To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we formally verify a LTL model checker with partial order reduction that can be implemented using a stepwise approach, that is, by generating executable code from a formal specification.

we have developed a formally verified and on-the-fly executable LTL model checker with ample set partial order reductions that uses a static partial order reduction algorithm and a stepwise refinement to generate executable code from a high-level description.
we have verified a formally correct on-the-fly LTA model checker that uses partial order reduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an executable model checking framework that is formally verified and that can be used as an alternative to the existing, non-executable model checkers.
the formal verification of a partial order reduction algorithm for a fragment of Promela that is sufficient for LTL model checking.
a formalization of the correctness of a partial order reduction algorithm for a Promela model checker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the verification and the generated SML implementation of an ample set LTL model checker is correct and efficient.
the correctness proofs and the code generation for the LTL model checker with ample set partial order are correct.
the model checker is correct and works as expected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we verified the correctness of a reduction algorithm for Promela, which is a subset of Promela that can be translated to LTL formulas, and that the resulting model checker works in practice.

we have formally verified a model checking tool that can check large state spaces, and the verification is complete in the sense that it covers everything from the model checker’s correctness down to its executable code.
we have verified the correctness of the LTL semantics and of ample set partial-order reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain formally verified executable code from a proof assistant by combining the strengths of the proof assistant and a high-level language.
it is possible to formally verify an LTL model checker with partial order reduction, from the abstract correctness theorem down to an executable SML implementation.
we can verify a complex model checking algorithm with partial order reduction, including a back end model checker, using a proof assistant.
